_comment: The 'Week Ahead' intro for the weekly email. Edit this file — no code change needed. Each key is the week-start date (the Monday the email covers, YYYY-MM-DD); the Saturday workflow computes that automatically. Add a new dated entry before each week's send. If a week has no entry, the email uses 'default'.
default: A fresh week across the box canyon — public meetings, community events, and a few ways to get involved are all below.
2026-06-15: The government calendar bunches up on Wednesday the 17th — Mountain Village Town Council, the San Miguel County Commissioners, and Telluride’s HARC all meet the same day, so if land use and what gets built next is your thing, that’s the day to show up. Norwood’s Planning and Zoning Commission kicks the week off on Monday, Ridgway’s Town Council holds a special meeting Tuesday, and summer is hitting full stride across the box canyon.
2026-06-22: A quieter week on the government calendar, but two items worth your time: on Tuesday afternoon, HARC and Planning & Zoning meet jointly to start lining Telluride’s code up with Colorado’s new Wildfire Resiliency Code (in effect July 1) — a piece of housekeeping that will quietly shape what gets built in the next decade. On Thursday, P&Z opens a work session on the Shandoka Lot proposed 900-space parking structure, the largest town-owned project on the boards right now. Out in the rest of the valley, the Yoga Festival lands Thursday through Sunday and summer hits its full mid-week rhythm.
2026-07-06: The week after the Fourth eases off a little, but the county’s land-use calendar doesn’t take the holiday off: the San Miguel County Commissioners hold a work session Wednesday, the Planning Commission meets Thursday, and Ridgway’s Town Council sits Wednesday too. Several of those agendas were still trickling in over the weekend, so check the Gov-Hub before you head down. Out in the box canyon, summer is hitting its stride — Music on the Green returns to Mountain Village on Friday and the North Mississippi Allstars play the Sheridan on Saturday.
2026-09-21: Tuesday is the big one — the **Telluride Housing Authority** and **Town Council** both take up a deed-restriction change for two units at 215 East Colorado Avenue, stripping the price cap and converting them from affordable ownership to employee dwelling units. Monday, Norwood's **Planning and Zoning Commission** opens the first phase of its Land Use Code rewrite — the kind of update that sets development rules for years. Wednesday, the **San Miguel County Board of County Commissioners** continues its public hearing on adopting updated building codes, and Thursday brings an early work session at Telluride's **Planning & Zoning Commission** on a proposed employee-housing project at the middle-high school site. On the lighter side: a guided **Bike & Brewery Tour** rolls out of Mountain Village Monday, **Photon** brings its Stephen-Hawking-inspired electronic show to The Alibi Thursday, and **Slap Dragon** closes out the week with acoustic-funk-disco at the Sherbino in Ridgway on Sunday.
2026-10-26:
Monday, the **SMART Gondola Advisory Committee** gets a status update on the federal Capital Investment Program funding that the gondola replacement depends on; no votes are planned. The **San Miguel Basin Fair Board** takes an early look at its 2027 budget, and the **San Miguel County Open Space Commission** also meets.
Tuesday, the **Telluride Town Council** is the one to watch. It takes up the Fourth Supplement to the Gondola IGA, which extends cost-sharing for 2027 planning on the gondola replacement, and gives first reading to two ordinances: one amending the Telluride Energy Mitigation Program, the other suspending the 5% capital fund allocation for open space in 2027. In Ridgway, the **Ouray County Board of County Commissioners** considers a fifth extension of the county's emergency disaster declaration, and its afternoon work session takes up the proposed merger of EMS with Ridgway Fire.
Wednesday, CDOT briefs the **Ouray County Board of County Commissioners** on plans for the US-550 corridor, followed by an update on FEMA recovery projects. The **San Miguel County Board of County Commissioners** holds an evening work session; its agenda hasn't been posted yet.
2026-11-02:
Monday evening, **Ouray City Council** holds its regular meeting with the 2027 budget as the main item of business, and the **Norwood Water Commission** sits down for a work session to sort through its own 2027 draft budget numbers well ahead of any formal vote.
Tuesday, the **Telluride Medical Center** board holds a special meeting to consider hiring Jensen Partners to guide its due diligence with CommonSpirit Health, a sign that a potential partnership or affiliation is being evaluated seriously. CommonSpirit Health was formed in 2019 as a national alignment of major hospital systems, one of the largest nonprofit hospital systems in the country.
Wednesday, the **San Miguel County Board of County Commissioners** holds its regular meeting, covering a 2027 fee schedule for vegetation control and management, a resolution setting next year's meeting calendar, a professional services agreement to digitize Planning Department files, a quarterly update from the Tres Rios BLM Field Office, and a motion to sign on to a letter opposing legal immunity for Big Oil; sitting as the county housing authority, it also takes up new administrative fees for housing programs. Also Wednesday, the **Telluride Board of Education** holds a work session to interview student candidates for the Student Representative seat, and the **Telluride Ecology Commission** meets with no agenda posted.
Thursday, the **Mountain Village Design Review Board** meets, though nothing of broad public consequence is on its agenda, and Telluride’s **Planning & Zoning Commission** holds a special meeting (no agenda posted yet).
2026-11-09:
Monday, the **Telluride Intergovernmental Meeting** gets the week started, joined by the **Telluride Open Space Commission**, which has three items on its agenda, and the **San Miguel Basin Fair Board**, which has no posted agenda.
Tuesday, over in Ouray County, the **Ouray County Board of County Commissioners** meets at 9 AM with two public hearings on its agenda, including a 2026 budget amendment and the Curry Regular PUD, a request to subdivide a 14.42-acre parcel on County Road 1 into two lots and open space; at 3 PM, the **Ouray County Board of County Commissioners Work Session** takes up back-to-back presentations from EcoAction Partners and San Miguel Power Association covering energy and environmental programming. Also Tuesday, the **Ouray Planning Commission** takes up two substantive matters, and the **Norwood Water Commission Meeting** convenes with no posted agenda.
Wednesday, the **Ridgway Town Council** and the **Norwood Board of Trustees** both meet with no posted agendas.
Thursday is the week's most consequential day. The **San Miguel County Planning Commission** holds a morning work session on proposed amendments to the Affordable Housing Impact Mitigation Fee — a structure that directly shapes whether and how workforce housing gets built across the county — along with a broader discussion of housing incentive ideas; after lunch, the commission takes up a county-initiated rezoning of a portion of Placerville Park near the fire station to bring its zoning in line with its actual public use. The **SMART Board of Directors** also meets Thursday with no posted agenda.
2026-11-16:
Monday, the **SMART Gondola Advisory Committee** meets at 3:00 PM, and the **Telluride Board of Education** holds a 3:30 PM work session on its retreat follow-up and strategic financial planning. At 4:00 PM, the **San Miguel County Open Space Commission** brings a full slate of trail, park and conservation updates. The **Ouray City Council Regular Meeting** opens at 6:00 PM with the 2027 budget as its centerpiece: four linked resolutions covering budget adoption, fund appropriations, the mill levy and the 2027 fee schedule. At 6:30 PM, the **Norwood Planning and Zoning Commission** takes up two foundational documents — a Land Use Code update and a Master Plan update — that will shape what gets built where for years to come.
Tuesday is the week’s busiest day. The **Ouray County Board of County Commissioners** meets at 9:00 AM, with two resolutions worth watching: one repealing the county’s existing austerity measures and one adopting formal AI policy and governance standards, one of the first such moves in the region. At 10:00 AM, **Telluride Town Council** takes up the 2027 budget and the property tax levy that funds it, alongside the second reading of an ordinance that would suspend the 5% Open Space Fund dedication from Real Estate Transfer Tax revenue for the coming year — a recurring tension between fiscal pressure and long-standing land-conservation commitments. Next will be a second reading of amendments to the Telluride Energy Mitigation Program, with a companion action updating TEMP’s energy offset fee calculator. At 10:05 AM, the **Telluride Housing Authority** conducts Master Lease lottery drawings for employee rentals at two Black Bear Road properties. At 5:15 PM, the **Telluride Board of Education** holds its monthly meeting, with a debrief on the November ballot measures, flood expense estimates and the choice of a superintendent search consultant. The **Telluride Fire District Board of Directors** follows at 5:30 PM with no posted agenda, and the **Ophir General Assembly** also meets Tuesday, with no agenda posted.
Wednesday, the **Ouray County Board of County Commissioners Work Session** opens at 9:00 AM with an EMS director quarterly update and discussion of an intergovernmental agreement between the county and Ridgway Fire. If adopted, this would mark a historic milestone for Ouray County by creating its first unified fire and EMS authority, transforming long-fragmented local services into a coordinated regional system. At 9:30 AM, the **San Miguel County Board of County Commissioners** meets in Norwood, though no agenda detail has been posted. At noon, **Telluride Parks & Recreation Commission** takes up a proposed update to the Town Park Pavilion Banner Policy that would add a category for Telluride High School senior winter sports athletes. The evening’s main event is the **Telluride Historic and Architectural Review Commission (HARC) Meeting** at 5:30 PM, with a heavy agenda: preliminary large-scale design reviews for the long-awaited Shandoka Lot redevelopment at 860 Black Bear Road, plus two other Town-owned sites — Rebekah Hall at 113 W Columbia, where demolition of the existing structure and new construction over 5,000 square feet are proposed, and 335 W Colorado, where a Landmark District primary structure faces demolition alongside large-scale new construction and relocation of two historic sheds. The **Rico Board of Trustees Regular Meeting** also convenes Wednesday at 7:00 PM with no agenda posted.
Thursday, the **Telluride Medical Center Regular Board Meeting** runs from 8:30 to 11:30 AM with no posted agenda. At noon, the **Telluride Regional Airport Authority (TRAA) Board of Commissioners Meeting** convenes with no agenda posted. At 3:00 PM, the **Mountain Village Town Council Meeting** carries the week’s major budget actions: a public hearing on the Mountain Village Metro District’s proposed 2027 budget; first readings on both the 2027 Town budget ordinance and the 2026 property tax levy ordinance; and adoption of the 2027 fee schedules. Two work sessions add further weight — one on a draft sewer authority agreement with Telluride for a new regional wastewater treatment plant, and one checking in on the Rural Homes Ilium affordable housing feasibility study. The evening closes with an executive session on the ongoing Sunset Concert litigation. At 4:00 PM, the **Telluride Resident Advisory Committee** meets with no posted agenda. At 5:30 PM, **Telluride Planning & Zoning Commission** hears a presentation on wildfire modeling technologies; continues a work session on potential Land Use Code amendments to landscaping and tree maintenance rules; and elects a new chair and vice chair.
